answer: An agent economy can resist sybils through age-weighted identity vesting. A fresh agent stays dormant and only earns economic weight after surviving unrevoked for a stretching period. To flood the network, an attacker must keep each fake alive for weeks-an oasis of patience few can afford. Trusted hardware forms the copper backbone, while a crystal of signed history lets peers confirm maturity instantly. The attacker's true cost becomes time and detection risk, not mere token spend.
